prompt: Start a worker Thread that computes a square into a shared array, join it, and return the result. Complete the computeInThread method in the starter file.
explanation: A Thread runs a Runnable in parallel with the caller; start() begins it and join() blocks until it finishes. Because a lambda cannot assign to a local variable, a shared one-element array is the classic way to carry a result out of a Runnable. join() also establishes a happens-before relationship, so the value written by the worker is guaranteed to be visible after the join.
hints: Create int[] result = new int[1]; a lambda can write into an array element even though it cannot reassign a local variable.
Build the thread with new Thread(() -> result[0] = n * n), then call start() on it.
Call worker.join() before returning result[0] -- without the join, the thread may not have finished writing yet.
